title: Introduce multi-tenant benchmark runner and profile->report pipeline
author: Priya Agarwal
description: Motivation: Our existing benchmark lab lacked a lightweight multi-tenant workload runner and an automated pipeline to turn collected CPU/GPU profiles into consumable performance reports. This PR adds a representative multi-tenant runner (emulates mixed short/long sequences and concurrent clients), integrated sampling/profile capture (perf, py-spy, nvprof hooks), and a reporting pipeline that aggregates profiles into per-run flamegraphs and a summarized CSV uploaded to S3. Changes are designed to be opt-in via BENCH_* env vars so the runner can be used in CI and by engineers locally. Key outcomes: 1) a repeatable workload for comparing batching/kv-cache strategies across model variants, 2) automated flamegraph generation for each trial, 3) a simple CSV/JSON summary that feeds our perf dashboard ingestion job. How to run: BENCH_MODE=multi_tenant python bench/run/multi_tenant_runner.py --config bench/configs/multi_tenant_demo.yaml ; perf artifacts land in ./bench/artifacts/<timestamp> and are uploaded when BENCH_S3_BUCKET is set. Rollout: staged to benchmark-lab nightly workflows first (disabled by default), then enable on perf-canary schedules. Backwards compatibility: none of the new modules are imported by default; existing bench scripts unchanged.

Priya Agarwal: Reply - lowered durations in multi_tenant_demo.yaml and added a helper to set CPU quota in ci/workflows. Added note about noisy-neighbor mitigation in docs.

testing_notes: Local smoke tested on x86 instance and G4. Flamegraphs produced by bench/reporting/generate_flamegraphs.sh matched expectations; summarize_reports.py creates CSV rows: run_id,model,threads,mean_latency,p50,p90,p99,token_rate,profile_path. Uploads only when BENCH_S3_BUCKET set and AWS creds present.

release_notes: Adds a multi-tenant workload runner and automated profile->flamegraph reporting pipeline for benchmark-lab. Useful for comparing batching and cache strategies across models; opt-in S3 uploads for perf dashboards.
